title: Digital Impacts Schema and Taxonomy (DIST) v0.0.1
description: A single-file schema for reporting the impacts of a technology estate across multiple dimensions. Each impact is recorded as an individual entry in the impacts array, allowing reporting at any level of granularity from a single top-level dimension figure down to a specific technology category.

$schema.description: The URL to the JSON schema file for the version of DIST you are using

description.description: Brief description of the organization, it's purpose and role, and  its technology estate.
examples: The Green Web Foundation is a non-profit organization working towards a fossil-free internet by 2030.

open_corporates_url.description: Open Corporates URL for the reporting organization, providing a verifiable corporate identity.

country.description: A valid [3-digit ISO 3166 alpha-3 country code](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search) for the country of registration of this organization

sector.description: Primary sector, according to the [SNA 2008](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/sna.asp) / [ESA 2010](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/esa-2010) standard categories for national accounting.

industries.description: Industrial sector according to the [ISICv5](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/classifications/Econ/isic) / [NACE](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/nace) categories. These can be a general section e.g. `"K"` (Telecommunications, computer programming, consultancy, computing infrastructure, and other information service activities), a division within that section, e.g. `"K62"` (Computer programming, consultancy and related activities), or a more specific class within that division, e.g. `"K6211"` (Development of video games, video game software, and video game software tools). The full classification is available at the ISIC link above.

activity_description.description: A text description of the activities the organization carries out. This may supplement the "sector" and "industries" fields with additional details,, or be used instead of them.
examples: Technology development, policy analysis and advocacy
Development of web applications and services

size.description: Employee count range, based on [Eurostat employment size classes](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/SBS_SC_IND_R2/default/table?lang=en).

report.description: A single impacts report covering a defined period.

reporting_period.description: The period over which impacts were measured or estimated, as ISO8601 format dates (YYYY-MM-DD).

verification.description: The level of verification applied to this report: `self_reported` if no independent verification has been carried out, `peer_reviewed` if the figures and methodology have been verified by independent, informal peer review, or `independently verified` if the impacts have been formally audited, validated, or certified by a third party.

verifier.description: Verifying organization. Required when verification is 'independently_verified'.

name.description: The name of the verifying organization

impacts.description: Individual impact measurements, organised by particular impact dimension being measured. Each dimension is optional - the absence of a dimension implies that that dimension has not been measured, not that no impact exists. For the moment DIST supports only the 'carbon' dimension - in future versions, other impacts such as 'water', 'energy', and 'health' will be added, once measurement methodology for each of these has been settled upon.

carbon.description: Array of individual co2e impact measurements. Each entry reports a single quantifiable impact. Report at whatever granularity you have data for. The absence of a category does not imply that the impact of that category is 0, but that no measurement is available. Categories with a 0 impact should be explicitly listed

categories.description: Array of category identiers from the [DIST taxonomy](https://dist.greenweb.org/taxonomy).

value.description: The measured or estimated impact value. An explicit `null` here indidates that an impact exists, but could not be measured, and therefore should be interpreted as 'unknown', rather than 'zero'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement of the value.

methodology_description.description: Human-readable description of the methodology used to calculate this value.

anyOf.description: Calculations that use real, device-specific primary data (manufacturer Product Carbon Footprint datasheets, actual usage data) with a clear, documented methodology count as high confidence numbers.

Medium confidence measurements also follow a documented methodology, and make clear any assumptions which go into their calculation, but may rely on generalisations or estimates where real product-level data is unavailable.

Low confidence measurements are those which result from larger assumptions or estimates, or from a less robust methodology. This might include stacking models (using one estimate as input to another estimation model), using very uncertain sources of data, or using proxies - taking data from one provider as an estimate for the impact of another.

confidence.description: Confidence in the reported value, this can be classified as low, medium, or high, depending on the specific methodology used, following the [guidelines on confidence](https://dist.greenweb.org/schema/confidence).

notes.description: Supporting notes: assumptions, scope boundaries, limitations, or anything a reader needs to interpret this value correctly.

data_sources.description: References to data sources used (URLs, document names, database identifiers).
